subtitle: Unofficial Chautauqua guide
promotionalText: New in 1.1.4: browse last season from the pre-season countdown, and ask Siri for a day even while you're parked on another year.
disclaimer: CHQ Calendar is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Chautauqua Institution. Event information is drawn from publicly posted listings; chq.org remains the authoritative source.
description:
CHQ Calendar is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Chautauqua Institution. Event information is drawn from publicly posted listings; chq.org remains the authoritative source.

Planning a day on the grounds shouldn't take longer than the day itself.

CHQ Calendar puts the whole Chautauqua season in one place, then helps you act on it — reminders for what you've starred, a plan for your day, and a map to get there.

NEVER MISS WHAT YOU STARRED
• Star an event to get a reminder — 30 minutes before, 1 hour before, or the night before
• Set a default reminder timing once, or override it per event
• Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets show what's next on the grounds, or just your starred events
• Widgets are configurable by venue, category, or starred-only

PLAN YOUR DAY
• My Day lays your starred events out on a timeline
• Flags schedule overlaps and tight walking gaps between venues
• Updates automatically as you star or unstar events

FIND YOUR WAY
• Every venue on the grounds plotted on a map
• Tap a venue for its next events and walking directions
• Jump to the map from any event's detail screen
• No location permission required

BROWSE THE SEASON
• Every event of the season, grouped by day
• A day rail above the list jumps you straight to any day with events; the list grows automatically as you reach the end
• Filter by category, venue, and week; search by name, venue, or presenter
• Full event details, including linked Chautauquan Daily articles
• Save favorites so you don't lose track of what you can't miss

WORKS EVERYWHERE
• Events you've already loaded stay readable offline
• Built for both iPhone and iPad
• Ask Siri — say “Chautauqua” and ask what’s next, what’s on tonight, who’s speaking, this week’s theme, or to show you a day
• Find events instantly from system-wide Spotlight search
• Quick links to Chautauqua’s own services, including live captioning for attendees who are deaf or hard of hearing
• Off-season, see a countdown to next season, browse announced events, and revisit past seasons

No account. No ads. No third-party trackers. Your filters, favorites, and reminders stay on your device.

Event information comes from publicly posted Chautauqua Institution listings and from local organizations that publish their own events. For ticketing, official announcements, and the last word on any event, visit chq.org.
whatsNew:
Version 1.1.4 fixes two places where the app knew about more than one Chautauqua season but would not take you to the right one.

ASK SIRI FOR A DAY FROM ANOTHER SEASON
• “Show me tomorrow in Chautauqua” now works while you are browsing a past season — the app switches to the right season and takes you to that day
• Before, Siri would say it was opening the day and the screen would not move

BROWSE A PAST SEASON WHILE YOU WAIT
• While a season has been announced but its schedule has not been published yet, the countdown screen now offers a button to browse the most recent season the app does have a schedule for
• Tapping it switches to that season and opens it, so there is something to read while you wait
• The button appears only when there is an earlier season to show
reviewNotes:
CHQ Calendar is an unofficial, independent app, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Chautauqua Institution — stated in the description's first paragraph, the About screen (toolbar > info button), and https://www.chqcal.org/privacy.

The app displays publicly posted event information for the Chautauqua Institution summer season — dates, times, titles, venues, presenters. Every event links back to chq.org, the authoritative source. Data is served from https://www.chqcal.org, operated by the developer.

No account or login is required. There is no gated content and no demo credentials are needed — launching the app shows the full feature set immediately.

The app contains no analytics or tracking SDKs and no advertising identifiers, and has no accounts — preferences and cached event data stay on device; calendar access is write-only, used only for events the user chooses to add. The website serving the app's data, https://www.chqcal.org, keeps standard CDN access logs and derives a pseudonymous key from IP address and user-agent to count unique and returning visitors in aggregate — declared in App Privacy as Usage Data (Product Interaction): not linked to identity, not used for tracking, never shared with third parties.

iOS-specific capabilities, introduced in 1.1 as the response to the prior 4.2 review and extended since: every item below is reachable within seconds of launch, no configuration required to see it exists.

- Reminders — star an event, then set "Remind me" in the event detail screen (30 min or 1 hour before, or 8 PM the night before).

- Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets — "Next Up" and "Starred", added from the iOS widget gallery under CHQ Calendar.

- My Day tab — starred events on a timeline, flagging schedule overlaps and tight walking gaps between venues.

- Map tab — every venue plotted, with that venue's next events and walking directions via Apple Maps. No location permission requested.

- Day rail — day chips above the events list. Tap a chip with events to jump to that day; empty chips are visible but disabled by design (disablesEmptyDays: true). ⟳ Now returns to today. A week band above the chips marks each Chautauqua week; tapping it jumps to the Saturday opening that week (or the first day in it with events, or nothing if none), without touching filters. VoiceOver reaches the same day-with-events step via a rotor action. The window grows forward automatically while scrolling; going back is a chip or band tap.

- Search and Filters — toolbar buttons beside the year and the ⋯ menu. Search scrolls away while reading — tap the magnifying glass to bring it back; it stays visible whenever a search term is active. Filters is one sheet: category, venue, week, and (under "When") the four date scopes.

- Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight — eight Shortcuts actions in the Shortcuts app under CHQ Calendar, each also runs by voice through Siri (also answers to "Chautauqua" and "CHQ"). "Show a Day" is the voice equivalent of a rail-chip tap — e.g. "Show me tomorrow in Chautauqua". New in 1.1.4: asking while parked on an archived season now switches to that day's season (#253); a day outside the current season's range is still declined with a spoken line. Unlike the rail (disablesEmptyDays, above), Siri can open a day with zero events, or one an active filter empties — by design, not a bug. Spotlight indexes the season's events plus every starred event; a tapped result opens directly to it.

- Off-season — outside the season the app shows a countdown to next season, a preview of its events once published, and browsable past seasons instead of an empty screen. In 1.1.4 the "Browse the [year] season" button also appears before a season opens (#186).

New in 1.1.4 vs 1.1.3: the pre-season "Browse the [year] season" button (#186) and "Show a Day" crossing seasons (#253), both above. No new permissions or data collection; everything above uses local notifications only — no push, no server-side scheduling.
